question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}({x}^{3}+y),\, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{14}{25}$ and $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{19}{15},$ calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The covariance of $X$ and $Y$ can be calculated using the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

To find $\text{E}[XY],$ we use the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}xyf(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}xy\cdot \frac{2}{5}({x}^{3}+y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{2}{5}y{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}+xy)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{2}{5}y{[\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}y]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{2}{5}y[\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{2}y]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{2}{25}y+\frac{1}{5}{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{25}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{15}{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{52}{75}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the covariance formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{52}{75}-(\frac{14}{25})(\frac{19}{15}) \\  & =-\frac{2}{125}.\end{aligned}
$$
